standard.title: Science and Technology Advance Together
standard.description: investigate how advances in technologies enable advances in science, and how science has contributed to developments in technologies and engineering
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can explain how scientific understanding has developed through people's questions, observations and experiments (AC9S7H03, AC9S7H04). They have not yet examined the two-way relationship between science and technology specifically — where technology enables scientific discovery and scientific understanding enables technological development — as a systematic relationship rather than individual historical examples.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate the two-directional relationship between science and technology — describing cases where technological advances enabled new scientific knowledge (imaging technologies, particle accelerators, digital monitoring tools) and cases where scientific understanding enabled technological development (radioactivity → medical imaging; wave-particle model → EM communications). Students can examine how this relationship has operated in Australian and global contexts.

nodes.label: Technology enabling science
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe cases where advances in technology enabled advances in scientific understanding — explaining what the technology made possible that was not possible before.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe one example where a technology enabled a scientific advance (e.g. development of imaging technologies enabling understanding of body system interactions; electron microscope enabling understanding of cell ultrastructure) and explain what the technology specifically made possible.
nodes.typical_width: Describe two or three cases of technology enabling science across different fields, explaining in each case what question or observation became possible with the new technology — connecting the tool to the knowledge it produced.
wider: Examine how modern technology has enabled exploration of energy conversion processes at scales previously inaccessible — from black holes to atoms to sub-atomic particles — as cases where the limits of scientific knowledge coincide with the limits of available technology.

Investigate how technological advances in monitoring greenhouse gas emissions and environmental factors have contributed to the reinstatement of traditional fire management practices — connecting remote sensing technology to both scientific knowledge and First Nations knowledge validation.
success_criteria: Can describe at least one example where technology enabled a scientific advance.
Can explain what the technology specifically made possible — not just that 'it helped'.
Does not treat the relationship as simply 'scientists use tools' — understands that the tool opened a previously inaccessible domain.

nodes.label: Science enabling technology
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe cases where scientific understanding enabled the development of new technologies or engineering solutions — explaining how the science provided the theoretical foundation for the technology.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe one example where scientific understanding directly enabled a technological application (e.g. understanding of radioactivity → radioisotope medical imaging; understanding of EM radiation properties → radar/mobile communications) and explain the specific connection.
nodes.typical_width: Describe two or three cases of science enabling technology across different content areas (biological, physical, chemical sciences), explaining in each case how understanding a mechanism or property made a specific technology possible.
wider: Investigate Australian technological contributions — cochlear implant (Graeme Clark), spray-on skin (Fiona Woods), wi-fi (O'Sullivan/CSIRO) — examining both the scientific understanding that underpinned each and how they generated new engineering knowledge.

Examine how understanding of radioactivity and radioisotopes has led to new applications and technologies — including medical diagnosis (PET scans, radioiodine therapy), industrial testing (checking welds in aircraft), and radiocarbon dating.

response_modes.reason: Vary the technology examples across biology, physics and materials science — Australian and international — to build genuine breadth in understanding the science-enables-technology direction. Single-domain examples (e.g. only medical technology) produce an incomplete picture.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of Australian technological developments offers genuine richness — students can examine cases across biology, physics and materials science, connecting diverse scientific understanding to engineering outcomes. The Australian context also builds awareness of local scientific contributions without forcing cultural tokenism.
success_criteria: Can describe at least one example where scientific understanding enabled a technological development.
Can explain the specific connection — what understanding made the technology possible.
Does not treat science and technology as sequential ('science first, then technology') — can recognise cases of mutual enablement.

nodes.label: The two-way relationship
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate the two-directional relationship between science and technology — recognising that the relationship is iterative, not sequential, and can examine multiple cases where each has enabled the other in a cycle of development.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe one domain where technology and science have advanced each other iteratively (e.g. medical imaging: understanding of EM radiation → X-ray technology → MRI understanding → MRI technology → new anatomical knowledge) and explain why the relationship is described as two-directional.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate two or three domains where science and technology have advanced each other across multiple iterations, and explain how scientists and engineers make machines or processes more efficient using scientific understanding as the lever.
wider: Examine how scientists and engineers make machines more energy efficient — connecting AC9S9U05 (conservation of energy, Sankey diagrams) to the applied science of engineering design.

Investigate how understanding of the nature of matter and energy has changed over time — from classical mechanics to quantum mechanics — and how each theoretical advance enabled new technologies (transistors, lasers, MRI) that in turn revealed new science.

response_modes.reason: The two-way relationship is the integrative claim of this descriptor. Students who have described individual cases of technology-enabling-science (Node 1) and science-enabling-technology (Node 2) need to coordinate these into a general claim: the relationship is reciprocal and iterative. The integration is conceptual — seeing the pattern across cases, not just collecting examples.

success_criteria: Can explain what 'two-directional' means in the science-technology relationship — not just state it.
Can provide an example where both directions are visible — technology enabling science AND science enabling technology in the same domain.
Does not treat the relationship as sequential — understands it as iterative and ongoing.
